svg.title: Backlog Item Anatomy
svg.desc: A3 landscape reference poster: definitions, templates, and good and weak examples of an epic, a feature and a story, using one running example, plus INVEST, acceptance criteria, and other backlog item types.
svg.text: What a good epic, feature and story look like, with one running example from big bet to thin slice.
Break Down Work · Epics, Features & Stories · INVEST (Bill Wake) · Given / When / Then
✓ Good example, and why it works
An online grocery service wants more customers to come back and order again. Follow it down the levels.
A big bet that should deliver a business
WEEKS TO MONTHS · OFTEN SEVERAL TEAMS
We believe making it quick to repeat a past order, for
returning customers, will increase repeat orders. We'll know
when weekly repeat orders rise from 22% to 30% in 3 months.
Names the people, the outcome and a measure, so it can be proven wrong.
A solution, not an outcome. No measure, so nobody can
tell if it worked, or when to stop.
Something users can see and use that
delivers part of the epic's value.
A FEW ITERATIONS · ONE OR TWO TEAMS
One-tap reorder of a past basket, so returning customers
can repeat a weekly shop in under a minute.
Usable on its own, with a clear benefit to a named user.
A technical layer. Nobody can use it alone, so it
delivers no value until everything else is done.
A thin, vertical slice of a feature that
a user can use. Finishes in days.
DAYS · WITHIN YOUR SLE · ONE TEAM
As a [type of user], I want [goal]
Independent · Negotiable · Valuable · Estimable · Small · Testable
As a returning customer, I want to see my last order on
the home page so that I can reorder it quickly.
Given I've ordered before, when I open the app,
then I see my last order with a Reorder button.
Given an item is out of stock, when I reorder,
Valuable to a user, small, and testable from the criteria.
“As a developer, I want a reorder
table so that the data is stored.”
No user value. It's a task
“As a customer, I want to reorder,
A step the team takes to finish a story.
Time-boxed research to answer a question.
Fix fast, or order it like any other item.
Technical work that makes future value possible, such as paying down debt.
“Who is this for, and what will be better for them?”
“Could a user use this slice on its own?”
Break Down Work · Vertical Slicing · Deliver Value Early
